title: Federal regulators shut $6 billion Indiana lender in biggest bank failure in over two years | CNN Business
text:
Source: CNN

Federal regulators shut down Indiana-based United Fidelity on Friday night, marking the biggest US bank failure since April 2024.

The Federal Deposit Insurance Corp.announcedthat First Citizens has agreed to assume all of United Fidelity’s deposits and assets.

FDIC officials saycustomers with depositsat United Fidelity will “retain all of their funds” as well as their deposit insurance coverage, now as customers of First Citizens, which also served as adistressed buyerin the larger Silicon Valley Bank failure of 2023.

Officials stressed that Friday evening and over the weekend, United Fidelity depositors can still access their funds, including by writing checks, visiting ATMs and using their debit cards.

In a sign of how distressed United Fidelity was when regulators decided to step in, the FDIC estimates the failure will wipe out $1.83 billion of the industry’s deposit insurance fund.

That represents an unusually high 31% loss on United Fidelity’s $5.9 billion in total assets as of the end of September.

In another likely sign of United Fidelity’s troubled state, First Citizens said it has only agreed to assume $4.5 billion of the bank’s deposits. That is well shy of the $5.4 billion the FDIC said United Fidelity held as of the end of September.

The FDIC said the deposit accounts that transfer to First Citizens exclude “certain brokered deposits” but did not disclose how many or why.

“We believe this transaction is both financially and strategically compelling,” First Citizens CEO Frank Holding Jr. said in a statement, “and we look forward to welcoming our new customers, earning their trust and positioning our company for continued success.”

First Citizens agreed to take on $3.1 billion of loans held by United Fidelity — but only at a steep discount. First Citizens said its winning bid included a deep asset discount of $2.6 billion, suggesting the lender is concerned the loans are troubled.

United Fidelity’s 22 branches across Indiana, Illinois, Florida, Colorado and the US Virgin Islands will reopen as First Citizens branches starting on Saturday, according to the FDIC.

It’s the biggest US bank failure since Philadelphia-based Republic Bank closed in April 2024 with $6 billion in assets, according to FDIC data.

United Fidelity becomes the second-biggest bank failure since the 2023 regional banking crisis that included the implosions of both Silicon Valley Bank and First Republic. Fearing other banks would go under next, US officials eventually stepped in with a rescue that helped prevent further failures.
